sermon.title: Season of Refreshing
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches on the times of refreshing that come from the presence of the Lord (Acts 3:19), tracing four awakenings in America (1730, 1790, 1856 and 1967): the conditions before each, what God did, and how men’s doctrines and extremes derailed them. He insists the credit belongs to Jesus, not flawed men or churches, and urges believers to seek a refreshing now by stirring one another up to love and good works.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: he gives “1 Chronicles 12:38” for the children of Issachar having understanding of the times; that verse is 1 Chronicles 12:32 (shown). The captions read “Hebrews 61” for repentance from dead works, rendered Hebrews 6:1. His historical figures and statements (colonial population and slave numbers, church attendance percentages, crowd sizes, Confederate soldiers saved, sexually transmitted disease rates, Catholics filled with the Spirit) and his comments on named historical preachers and church leaders are his own and are not verified here. A few words are marked [unclear].

faqs.question: What was the half covenant?
faqs.answer: He says the Puritans made a half covenant which allowed unsaved people to be members of the church without being born again or converted.

faqs.question: What humanist ideas does he say were growing before the first awakening?
faqs.answer: He says humanism taught “you can be good without God” and that there’s no power in prayer.

faqs.question: Who was leading people to Christ in the first awakening?
faqs.answer: He says thousands were converted by church members; they weren’t waiting for the ministers to do it, they had a personal relationship with Jesus, read their Bible and shared the gospel.

faqs.question: Is emotion in revival a fault?
faqs.answer: He says there was some emotional shaking, screaming and loud joy, and the Old Light said it was just emotion: “if that’s the worst fault you can find in God’s church we’re doing good.”

faqs.question: Should we be lifted up when God uses us?
faqs.answer: He says we should not get uplifted because God uses us or uplift people because God uses them; they are nothing, just like the donkey that talked to Balaam was used of God.

faqs.question: What is deism?
faqs.answer: He says deism is a belief in God but he has no power; God leaves us to make up our own mind.

faqs.question: What was the great disappointment of 1844?
faqs.answer: He says people predicted Christ would come in 1844; thousands sold their properties and even bought white robes, and when Christ did not come many mocked the church.

faqs.question: What sums up the whole Bible, according to him?
faqs.answer: He says the great commandment to love God, love your neighbor and love yourself by doing no harm “sums up the whole Bible.”

faqs.question: Does the church sometimes bring problems on itself?
faqs.answer: He says many people were cynical of the church after the great disappointment, and “sometimes the church brings problems on itself by extreme teachings.”

faqs.question: Do we win people to Christ only through relationships?
faqs.answer: He says emerging churches teach that you win people through relationship, but they forget the 3,000 in Acts 2 and the 5,000 in Acts 4 who had no relationship with anybody: God came and converted them.

faqs.question: Does the style of church music matter?
faqs.answer: He says the style of music should not be the issue; it should be music in which you can encounter the presence of Jesus Christ and be encouraged to love and to do good works.

faqs.question: What was the result of these refreshings?
faqs.answer: He says Bible morality and a personal encounter with Jesus are not popular, “but the results are indisputable”: each refreshing changed the church and impacted the whole nation.
